sentences.en: Hello, everybody.
sentences.zh: 大家好。

sentences.en: I'm Gemma Spake, and welcome back to The Psychology of Your 20s, the podcast where we talk through the biggest changes, moments, and transitions of our 20s,
sentences.zh: 我是 Gemma Spake，欢迎回到《二十岁的心理学》，这是一档探讨我们二十岁时所经历的最大变化、时刻和转折的播客，

sentences.en: and what they mean for our psychology.
sentences.zh: 以及这些经历对我们心理意味着什么。

sentences.en: Hello, everybody.
sentences.zh: 大家好。

sentences.en: Welcome back to the show.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到节目。

sentences.en: Welcome back to the podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到播客。

sentences.en: New listeners, old listeners, wherever you are in the world, it is so great to have you here back for another episode as we, of course,
sentences.zh: 无论你是新听众还是老听众，无论你身处世界何地，很高兴你能回来收听新的一期节目，当然，

sentences.en: Break Down the Psychology of Our 20s.
sentences.zh: 我们要继续剖析二十岁的心理学。

sentences.en: Today, I hope you are ready for a big episode, a very long episode, an incredibly interesting episode.
sentences.zh: 今天，希望你已经准备好迎接一期重磅、超长且极其有趣的节目了。

sentences.en: We are talking about the psychology of plastic surgery.
sentences.zh: 我们要聊的是整形手术背后的心理学。

sentences.en: We know that there is this huge intersection between plastic surgery and psychology, between plastic surgery and insecurity, social conditioning, social media, self-confidence,
sentences.zh: 我们知道整形手术与心理学之间存在巨大的交集，它与不安全感、社会条件反射、社交媒体、自信心紧密相连，

sentences.en: and sometimes it stirs up a lot of debate online and in our own conversations.
sentences.zh: 有时它也会在网络上和我们的日常对话中引发激烈的争论。

sentences.en: I've always wanted to do an episode on this, but I am not an expert, so I thought I would bring on somebody who most certainly is somebody who has decades of experience
sentences.zh: 我一直想做一期关于这个话题的节目，但我不是专家，所以我决定请来一位绝对的专家，一位在这一领域拥有数十年经验的人，

sentences.en: navigating this industry, navigating the emotions to do with plastic surgery, navigating every single little bit and part of, yeah, of this experience and of this process.
sentences.zh: 他深谙这个行业，了解与整形手术相关的情绪，熟悉这个体验和过程中的每一个细枝末节。

sentences.en: So I'm so excited to have him on board for a super interesting conversation.
sentences.zh: 所以我非常兴奋能邀请他加入，进行一场超级有趣的对话。

sentences.en: Whatever you believe, I just feel like you can learn so much from how he approaches this, what we talk about, the nooks and crannies that we get into.
sentences.zh: 无论你的观点如何，我觉得你都能从他的切入点、我们讨论的内容以及我们深入探讨的每一个细节中获益良多。

sentences.en: So without further ado, let's talk about the complex, interesting, incredibly fascinating psychology of plastic surgery.
sentences.zh: 那么，废话不多说，让我们来聊聊整形手术复杂、有趣且极其迷人的心理学。

sentences.en: Dr. Radhi Rabban, welcome to the show.
sentences.zh: Radhi Rabban 医生，欢迎来到节目。

sentences.en: Can you introduce yourself to the audience and just tell them a bit about who you are and what you do?
sentences.zh: 你能向听众介绍一下自己，并简单说说你是谁以及你是做什么的吗？

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然可以。

sentences.en: My name is Radhi Rabban.
sentences.zh: 我叫 Radhi Rabban。

sentences.en: I'm a board-certified plastic surgeon out of Beverly Hills in California in the United States.
sentences.zh: 我是美国加州比佛利山庄的一名委员会认证整形外科医生。

sentences.en: I've been a board-certified plastic surgeon practicing predominantly, I would say, aesthetic surgery for over 20 years in this sort of epicenter of Beverly Hills.
sentences.zh: 作为一名委员会认证的整形外科医生，我在比佛利山庄这个中心地带从事审美外科手术已经超过 20 年了。

sentences.en: And I've done, I kind of uniquely find myself
sentences.zh: 而且我发现自己比较独特的一点是，

sentences.en: doing all aspects of plastic surgery.
sentences.zh: 我涉猎整形手术的方方面面。

sentences.en: Usually the minute you tell someone you do plastic surgery, their next question is, oh, really?
sentences.zh: 通常你一告诉别人你是做整形手术的，他们的下一个问题就是：哦，真的吗？

sentences.en: Okay, great.
sentences.zh: 好的，太棒了。

sentences.en: What do you specialize in?
sentences.zh: 你擅长什么？

sentences.en: And I kind of find myself a little bit of a unicorn in that I literally do face, nose, eyelid, breasts, bellies, et cetera, et cetera.
sentences.zh: 我感觉自己有点像个“独角兽”，因为我确实做面部、鼻子、眼睑、胸部、腹部等等手术。

sentences.en: So I do the gamut of plastic surgery.
sentences.zh: 所以我涵盖了整形手术的方方面面。

sentences.en: This is a question I've always wanted to ask a plastic surgeon, which is how did you find yourself in this industry slash in this space?
sentences.zh: 这是一个我一直想问整形外科医生的问题：你是怎么进入这个行业或这个领域的？

sentences.en: Like when you went and did your MD or I don't know what the process is in the US, did you know you wanted to do plastic surgery or did you just kind of like trip and fall into it?
sentences.zh: 比如当你去读医学博士时，或者我不清楚美国的流程是什么，你是早就知道自己想做整形手术，还是误打误撞进来的？

sentences.en: That's a great question.
sentences.zh: 这是一个很好的问题。

sentences.en: The answer is that people go about it in both ways.
sentences.zh: 答案是，人们进入这个领域的方式各有不同。

sentences.en: Some people know early on, I would say most sort of find their selves trip and fall into it.
sentences.zh: 有些人很早就确定了，但我认为大多数人都是误打误撞进来的。

sentences.en: I always, always wanted to do something
sentences.zh: 我一直一直都想做一些

sentences.en: in design fusion with science.
sentences.zh: 将设计与科学融合在一起的事情。

sentences.en: You know, I actually wanted to be a mechanical engineer for a period of time and then I wanted to be an architect.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我曾经有一段时间想成为一名机械工程师，后来又想成为一名建筑师。

sentences.en: So plastic surgery was a, the minute I decided, I went to college at UCLA, which is down the street from my home.
sentences.zh: 所以整形手术是……我决定之后，就去了离家不远的加州大学洛杉矶分校（UCLA）上大学。

sentences.en: And I went in as a biochemistry major just simply because I liked science and science came pretty naturally to me.
sentences.zh: 我主修生物化学，仅仅是因为我喜欢科学，而且科学对我来说比较容易上手。

sentences.en: But I always knew that I needed to do something in the design, aesthetic, creative realm.
sentences.zh: 但我一直知道我需要从事设计、审美和创意领域的工作。

sentences.en: But I had a very strong liking towards the sciences, mechanical and civil engineering.
sentences.zh: 但我对科学、机械和土木工程也有着浓厚的兴趣。

sentences.en: So when you actually really, really think about it,
sentences.zh: 所以当你真正深入思考时，

sentences.en: plastic surgery is that beautiful fusion.
sentences.zh: 整形手术就是这种完美的融合。

sentences.en: And then I always loved entrepreneurship.
sentences.zh: 而且我一直热爱创业。

sentences.en: I love business.
sentences.zh: 我热爱商业。

sentences.en: I love, you know, VCs.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢风险投资。

sentences.en: I love Shark Tank.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢《创智赢家》（Shark Tank）。

sentences.en: And then when you think about plastic surgery, it is actually the perfect tricycle.
sentences.zh: 当你想到整形手术时，它实际上是一个完美的三轮车。

sentences.en: It's, you know, business, medicine,
sentences.zh: 它是商业、医学

sentences.en: and design all merged into one.
sentences.zh: 和设计的完美结合。

sentences.en: And for you to be arguably successful, you need to sort of excel in all three categories.
sentences.zh: 要取得成功，你必须在这三个领域都出类拔萃。

sentences.en: If you imagine one of those wheels being smaller than the others, you're not going to get very far.
sentences.zh: 如果你想象其中一个轮子比其他的小，你就走不远。

sentences.en: So it was actually the minute I got to undergrad, I knew pretty quickly that I wanted to do something in the medical space.
sentences.zh: 所以其实我一上大学，就很快意识到我想在医学领域做点什么。

sentences.en: And the only thing in medicine that allows you this degree of latitude in the creative element really is plastic surgery, not orthopedics, not OBGYN, not pediatrics.
sentences.zh: 而在医学领域，唯一能让你在创意元素上有如此大发挥空间的，真的只有整形手术，而不是骨科、妇产科或儿科。

sentences.en: So it was plastic surgery or buSt.
sentences.zh: 所以要么做整形手术，要么就放弃。

sentences.en: That's so interesting that you say it's like almost a creative part of medicine.
sentences.zh: 你说它是医学中近乎创意的一部分，这太有趣了。

sentences.en: And I feel like when I first hear that,
sentences.zh: 我感觉当我第一次听到这个说法时，

sentences.en: I'm like, wow, that sounds, that's like actually, that sounds strange.
sentences.zh: 我会觉得，哇，这听起来……实际上，这听起来很奇怪。

sentences.en: And then I'm like, well, yeah, you are.
sentences.zh: 然后我又想，嗯，确实是这样。

sentences.en: You're like sculpting the body and changing it to match someone's vision for how they want to look,
sentences.zh: 你就像是在雕刻身体，改变它以符合某人对自己外貌的愿景，

sentences.en: which is the fact that they're putting their care in your hands to execute their vision is also pretty amazing.
sentences.zh: 而他们把自己的身体交给你去实现他们的愿景，这本身也是一件非常了不起的事情。

sentences.en: Like there must be a great deal of trust in that as well for you to have these people come to you.
sentences.zh: 所以，这些人来找你，一定也包含了极大的信任。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, I actually take it with great reverence and a certain degree of stress associated with it.
sentences.zh: 是的，我确实怀着极大的敬畏之心，同时也伴随着一定程度的压力。

sentences.en: You know, I think the sign of a great surgeon is one who has a certain degree of humility and fear.
sentences.zh: 我认为一位伟大的外科医生的标志是拥有一定程度的谦逊和敬畏。

sentences.en: And that fear is, you know, you say people are God-fearing and that, you know, they have respect for something outside of themselves.
sentences.zh: 这种敬畏，就像人们说“敬畏上帝”一样，意味着他们对自身之外的事物怀有尊重。

sentences.en: And so when people come to you and they say, you know, whether it's a young girl or a young gentleman or an older person or what have you, and there's something about themselves
sentences.zh: 所以当人们来找你，无论是年轻女孩、年轻男士、年长者还是其他人，当他们觉得自己的某个部分

sentences.en: that doesn't, isn't congruent with the way they see themselves and they ask you to help them get there.
sentences.zh: 与他们对自己的认知不符，并请求你帮助他们达成目标时，

sentences.en: It's a very sizable responsibility.
sentences.zh: 这是一种非常沉重的责任。

sentences.en: And so I take it as such.
sentences.zh: 所以我就是这样对待它的。

sentences.en: So I have always been in awe with what I get to do on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 所以我一直对我每天所做的工作感到敬畏。

sentences.en: I never take it lightly.
sentences.zh: 我从不掉以轻心。

sentences.en: One more icebreaker question for you.
sentences.zh: 再问你一个破冰问题。

sentences.en: And I don't know if this is a weird question and you can not answer it if you don't want to.
sentences.zh: 我不知道这算不算奇怪的问题，如果你不想回答也可以不回答。

sentences.en: What was the first surgery that you performed as a plastic surgeon?
sentences.zh: 你作为整形外科医生做的第一台手术是什么？

sentences.en: Do you remember?
sentences.zh: 你还记得吗？

sentences.en: Of course I do.
sentences.zh: 我当然记得。

sentences.en: I remember it vividly.
sentences.zh: 我记得非常清楚。

sentences.en: So I've been in practice now 20 plus years and, you know, every pilot, every police officer, every person has a first of something, right?
sentences.zh: 我从业已经 20 多年了，你知道，每个飞行员、每个警察，每个人都有第一次，对吧？

sentences.en: The first time I fly a plane.
sentences.zh: 比如我第一次开飞机。

sentences.en: And you think to yourself like, okay, but like those other jobs, like who cares if you mess it up?
sentences.zh: 你会想，好吧，但像那些工作，搞砸了又怎样？

sentences.en: Who cares if you fuck it up?
sentences.zh: 搞砸了谁在乎呢？

sentences.en: But with surgery, the first person is, you know, you know, it's going to have to, is the one who, who, who is your icebreaker.
sentences.zh: 但对于手术来说，第一个病人，你知道的，那是你的破冰者。

sentences.en: So the first surgery I did actually was a breast augmentation.
sentences.zh: 所以我做的第一台手术其实是隆胸手术。

sentences.en: A very dear friend of mine who I adore and was at my wedding and is still a very close friend of mine, always had great faith in me.
sentences.zh: 我的一位挚友，我非常敬重她，她参加了我的婚礼，至今仍是我非常亲密的朋友，她一直对我很有信心。

sentences.en: And she sent me one of her friends who had had a few kids and I ended up doing a breast augmentation on her.
sentences.zh: 她给我介绍了一位生过几个孩子的朋友，我最终为她做了隆胸手术。

sentences.en: And I remember her very, very well because she was so sweet and so bubbly.
sentences.zh: 我记得她记得非常清楚，因为她非常甜美，性格也很开朗。

sentences.en: She had had four children.
sentences.zh: 她生了四个孩子。

sentences.en: And, uh, yeah, I did.
sentences.zh: 是的，我做了。

sentences.en: My first case was a breast first breast dog and, uh, it actually went quite well.
sentences.zh: 我的第一个病例是隆胸，而且手术进行得相当顺利。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: She's still sending me patients.
sentences.zh: 她现在还在给我介绍病人。

sentences.en: So I think it was a success.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为那是一次成功的手术。

sentences.en: Well, that's good.
sentences.zh: 那太好了。

sentences.en: Moving on to like the actual questions around the nitty gritty of, of plastic surgery.
sentences.zh: 接下来我们聊聊整形手术中更实际、更核心的问题。

sentences.en: One thing I feel like we need to get out of the way slash discuss discuss is the difference between plastic surgery and cosmetic procedures or cosmetic surgery.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我们需要先明确或讨论的一点是，整形手术（Plastic Surgery）和美容手术（Cosmetic Procedures/Surgery）之间的区别。

sentences.en: I'm of the, I feel like I think they're kind of different.
sentences.zh: 我感觉它们是不一样的。

sentences.en: Am I wrong in that?
sentences.zh: 我这样理解对吗？

sentences.en: Or are they quite similar?
sentences.zh: 还是说它们其实很相似？

sentences.en: So I think you ask a very good question.
sentences.zh: 你问了一个非常好的问题。

sentences.en: If the goal of today's episode is to educate and elevate people's understanding, then you got to understand the alphabet soup.
sentences.zh: 如果今天这期节目的目标是教育和提升人们的认知，那么你必须理解这些术语的“字母汤”。

sentences.en: You got to understand the vocabulary.
sentences.zh: 你必须理解词汇表。

sentences.en: You got to understand the glossary of plastic surgery.
sentences.zh: 你必须理解整形手术的术语。

sentences.en: And so unlike all other fields, plastic surgery is very confusing.
sentences.zh: 与其他领域不同，整形手术非常令人困惑。

sentences.en: And that's not by accident because ultimately a lot of it is driven by marketing, marketing.
sentences.zh: 这并非偶然，因为归根结底，很大程度上是由市场营销驱动的。

sentences.en: You don't get confused when you have an arrhythmia and your heart is not functioning.
sentences.zh: 当你心律失常、心脏功能异常时，你不会感到困惑。

sentences.en: Correct.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: You go to a cardiologiSt.
sentences.zh: 你会去看心脏病专家。

sentences.en: There's no confusion on that.
sentences.zh: 这一点毫无疑问。

sentences.en: When you have a ovarian cyst, you go to your OBGYN, your gynecologist, your obstetrician.
sentences.zh: 当你患有卵巢囊肿时，你会去看妇产科医生。

sentences.en: There's no confusion in that.
sentences.zh: 这一点也毫无疑问。

sentences.en: But in the area of cosmetics, my God, there are thousands of different providers with all kinds of names and things like that.
sentences.zh: 但在美容领域，天哪，有成千上万种不同的提供者，有着各种各样的头衔和名目。

sentences.en: So the way it works is as follows.
sentences.zh: 情况是这样的：

sentences.en: When you go, at least in the United States, when you go to medical school, you are all equal.
sentences.zh: 至少在美国，当你进入医学院时，大家的起点都是一样的。

sentences.en: And then you have to select a specialty.
sentences.zh: 然后你必须选择一个专业。

sentences.en: You say, okay, when I'm done with my four years of med school, I'm going to be a, again,
sentences.zh: 你会说，好吧，四年医学院毕业后，我要成为一名……再说一次，

sentences.en: orthopedist, neurologist, psychiatrist, blah, blah, blah, blah, blah, blah.
sentences.zh: 骨科医生、神经科医生、精神科医生等等等等。

sentences.en: And one of those is a plastic surgeon.
sentences.zh: 其中之一就是整形外科医生。

sentences.en: There is no cosmetic surgery residency.
sentences.zh: 并没有所谓的“美容外科”住院医师培训。

sentences.en: There is no, it's just plastic surgery.

sentences.zh: 事情不是这样发生的。

sentences.en: This is a person who has been dwelling on this subject matter for years, seeks out help, comes to the office.
sentences.zh: 这是一个多年来一直纠结于这个问题，寻求帮助，并来到办公室的人。

sentences.en: And I say, how can I help you?
sentences.zh: 我说，我能帮你什么吗？

sentences.en: And they say, well, I'm not so happy about my nose.
sentences.zh: 她们说，嗯，我对我的鼻子不太满意。

sentences.en: What is it about your nose that you dislike?
sentences.zh: 你对你的鼻子哪里不满意？

sentences.en: Well, I don't like this huge hump.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我不喜欢这个巨大的驼峰。

sentences.en: I don't like that it's droopy.
sentences.zh: 我不喜欢它下垂的样子。

sentences.en: I don't like that my tip is massively bulbous.
sentences.zh: 我不喜欢我的鼻尖看起来特别圆大。

sentences.en: And that doesn't make it bad.
sentences.zh: 这并不意味着它客观上“不好”。

sentences.en: That makes it bad to them.
sentences.zh: 这只是对她们来说“不好”。

sentences.en: There is no such thing as bad.
sentences.zh: 根本没有所谓的“不好”。

sentences.en: If that girl or that guy loved those features, then it would be good to them.
sentences.zh: 如果那个女孩或男孩喜欢那些特征，那对他们来说就是“好”。

sentences.en: So when I say bad or good, it's relative to the way they perceive themselves as to either what they would like and or what they used to be.
sentences.zh: 所以当我谈论好坏时，这是相对于他们如何看待自己，以及他们想要什么或曾经是什么样子的。

sentences.en: So then people who like to sort of be naysayers like to be like, well, what's wrong with it?
sentences.zh: 所以那些喜欢唱反调的人会说，嗯，这有什么问题吗？

sentences.en: Who says that a hump is bad?
sentences.zh: 谁说有驼峰就是不好？

sentences.en: And they like to sort of play that game.
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢玩这种文字游戏。

sentences.en: Then I ask you, why did you put on lipstick this morning?
sentences.zh: 那么我问你，你今天早上为什么要涂口红？

sentences.en: Are you wearing mascara?
sentences.zh: 你涂睫毛膏了吗？

sentences.en: Have you done your nails?
sentences.zh: 你做美甲了吗？

sentences.en: Do you cut your short, trim your split ends?
sentences.zh: 你剪短发、修剪分叉了吗？

sentences.en: Do you wear perfume?
sentences.zh: 你喷香水了吗？

sentences.en: Do you have jewelry?
sentences.zh: 你戴首饰了吗？

sentences.en: Under your arMs.
sentences.zh: 腋下呢？

sentences.en: So if we want to play that game, everyone will fail because it's not about the actual absolute, meaning this is okay and that's not because all that is is a line in the sand.
sentences.zh: 所以如果我们想玩那个游戏，每个人都会失败，因为这与绝对标准无关，即什么是对的，什么是错的，因为那不过是沙滩上的一条线。

sentences.en: Who are you to tell me that I'm allowed to put on mascara, but when I get a tattoo, I've gone too far.
sentences.zh: 你凭什么告诉我，我可以涂睫毛膏，但如果我纹身，就做得太过分了？

sentences.en: Who are you to tell me that I'm allowed to put Botox, but if I get a nose job, it's too far.
sentences.zh: 你凭什么告诉我，我可以打肉毒杆菌，但如果我做隆鼻手术，就太过分了？

sentences.en: No one can say that.
sentences.zh: 没有人能这么说。

sentences.en: It's about relativism and relativism is a dangerous area.
sentences.zh: 这是关于相对主义，而相对主义是一个危险的领域。

sentences.en: So because no one can make that definition, it's a slippery slope because the person who has had 47 surgeries can now reverse the argument like, so what?
sentences.zh: 所以因为没有人能做出那个定义，这是一个滑坡谬误，因为那个做了 47 次手术的人现在可以反驳说，那又怎样？

sentences.en: Who said 47 is bad?
sentences.zh: 谁说47岁不好？

sentences.en: Why?
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.en: Why is it only two?
sentences.zh: 为什么只有两个？

sentences.en: But we're talking about mentally stable, healthy individuals who look at themselves and feel, you know what?
sentences.zh: 但我们谈论的是那些心理稳定、健康的人，他们审视自己时会想，你知道吗？

sentences.en: I don't really love my saggy breasts.
sentences.zh: 我其实并不喜欢我那下垂的乳房。

sentences.en: And to them, it's bad.
sentences.zh: 对他们来说，这很糟糕。

sentences.en: And then there's people to them.
sentences.zh: 然后还有另一类人。

sentences.en: It's great.
sentences.zh: 这很棒。

sentences.en: And what we have to do as a society is make sure that we don't get too far off the spectrum.
sentences.zh: 作为社会，我们要做的是确保我们不会偏离正常范围太远。

sentences.en: And we were doing okay because, you know, at the end of the day, we had realistic images of what could be.
sentences.zh: 我们之前做得还不错，因为归根结底，我们对什么是可能的有现实的认知。

sentences.en: But I think the dangerous area or the dangerous waters we're in now is that things are so accessible.
sentences.zh: 但我认为我们现在所处的危险领域或危险水域是，事情变得太容易获取了。

sentences.en: You can go to Turkey.
sentences.zh: 你可以去土耳其。

sentences.en: You can go to downtown.
sentences.zh: 你可以去市中心。

sentences.en: You can go to Miami.
sentences.zh: 你可以去迈阿密。

sentences.en: Things have become relatively affordable, even though everybody bitches is expensive.
sentences.zh: 尽管每个人都在抱怨价格昂贵，但事情已经变得相对负担得起了。

sentences.en: I mean, you could literally go and get a boob job for nothing.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你真的可以随随便便去做个隆胸手术。

sentences.en: And images are endless.
sentences.zh: 而且图像层出不穷。

sentences.en: So this is a cocktail or a recipe for a very bad outcome.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个导致非常糟糕结果的鸡尾酒或配方。

sentences.en: Does that answer your question as to what defines the person as a bad nose or what my nieces felt was a bad nose?
sentences.zh: 这是否回答了你关于什么定义了一个人是“坏鼻子”，或者我侄女们觉得什么是“坏鼻子”的问题？

sentences.en: Yeah, it does.
sentences.zh: 是的，回答了。

sentences.en: And I think it's like a very, like you said, it's incredibly complicated.
sentences.zh: 而且我觉得这就像你说的，非常、非常复杂。

sentences.en: And I think the line some people would draw is that there's a difference between mascara and permanently altering how you look.
sentences.zh: 我认为有些人会划定的界限是，化妆和永久改变外貌之间是有区别的。

sentences.en: Like you can take the mascara off.
sentences.zh: 比如你可以卸掉睫毛膏。

sentences.en: You can't take the nose job off.
sentences.zh: 但你没法卸掉隆鼻手术。

sentences.en: What do you tell people with tattoos?
sentences.zh: 那你怎么看待纹身的人呢？

sentences.en: No, I know.
sentences.zh: 不，我知道。

sentences.en: I would have seen the same thing where it's like, I mean, tattoo, 85% of young adults, not it, not really.
sentences.zh: 我也会看到同样的情况，比如，纹身，85%的年轻人，不，其实不是。

sentences.en: No, that's a lie.
sentences.zh: 不，那是谎言。

sentences.en: Those are what people tell themselves.
sentences.zh: 那是人们对自己说的话。

sentences.en: But tattoos are essentially permanent.
sentences.zh: 但纹身本质上是永久的。

sentences.en: Even if you remove it, you have the scar of it.
sentences.zh: 即使你把它洗掉，也会留下疤痕。

sentences.en: And the reality is that, again, I agree with you.
sentences.zh: 事实是，我再次同意你的观点。

sentences.en: It's all a sense of relativism.
sentences.zh: 这全是一种相对主义的感觉。

sentences.en: And I think it's great to play devil's advocate because we need to make sure that we find center ground.
sentences.zh: 我认为扮演魔鬼代言人很好，因为我们需要确保找到中间立场。

sentences.en: Center ground is that we're not far left, we're not far right, whether that's in politics, whether that's in religion, and whether that's in plastic surgical philosophy.
sentences.zh: 中间立场就是我们既不极左，也不极右，无论是在政治、宗教还是整形外科哲学上。

sentences.en: So I do agree that each person will find that center area and draw that line.
sentences.zh: 所以我确实同意每个人都会找到那个中心区域并划定界限。

sentences.en: And yes, for someone, mascara is reversible, yet a tattoo is not.
sentences.zh: 是的，对某些人来说，睫毛膏是可逆的，而纹身则不然。

sentences.en: For some people, that too is not really reversible because I can cover it.
sentences.zh: 对有些人来说，纹身也不是真的不可逆，因为我可以遮盖它。

sentences.en: So there's all these versions of the way we sell it to ourselves.
sentences.zh: 所以我们有各种各样的说辞来让自己接受。

sentences.en: I think the key is, and it has been for me, because ultimately I'm the gatekeeper, right?
sentences.zh: 我认为关键在于——对我来说一直如此，因为归根结底我是把关人，对吧？

sentences.en: I'm the one that will facilitate this alteration in you.
sentences.zh: 我是那个将促成你这种改变的人。

sentences.en: So I take that responsibly quite heavily.
sentences.zh: 所以我非常认真地承担这份责任。

sentences.en: And there were many patients over the course of 20 years that I have redirected, re-advised, re-centered, and refused.
sentences.zh: 在过去的20年里，有很多病人被我劝导、重新建议、重新调整心态，甚至被我拒绝过。

sentences.en: Let's talk about those patients.
sentences.zh: 我们来谈谈那些病人吧。

sentences.en: Because I think regardless of, you know, if you're listening to this, regardless of whether you think plastic surgery is a good idea, you've had it done yourself,
sentences.zh: 因为我认为无论你是在听这个节目，无论你是否认为整形手术是个好主意，你自己是否做过，

sentences.en: or you're one of those people who's like, I would never do that.
sentences.zh: 或者你是那种说“我永远不会那样做”的人，

sentences.en: I want to go through the psychological process of loving my body as it is.
sentences.zh: 我想探讨一下爱自己身体的心理过程。

sentences.en: I think we can all kind of identify that there is a level where someone seeking out plastic surgery might be a little bit problematic.
sentences.zh: 我想我们都能认同，在某种程度上，寻求整形手术的人可能存在一点问题。

sentences.en: Can you tell me when you know, or instances where you've been like, this person is probably not a good candidate for plastic surgery?
sentences.zh: 你能告诉我你是怎么知道的，或者举些例子，说明你觉得某个人可能不是整形手术的好人选吗？

sentences.en: Great question.
sentences.zh: 好问题。

sentences.en: So first and foremost, my overall philosophy is not that plastic surgery is good for everyone.
sentences.zh: 首先，我的总体哲学并不是说整形手术对每个人都好。

sentences.en: As a matter of fact, absolutely, it's not good for everyone.
sentences.zh: 事实上，绝对不是对每个人都好。

sentences.en: My simple philosophy is that if you are the right candidate, and we've been sort of touching on what that is, and you do a good surgery,
sentences.zh: 我简单的哲学是，如果你是合适的人选——我们刚才一直在讨论什么是合适的人选——并且你做了好的手术，

sentences.en: and you find a good surgeon who collaborates with you, my experience for 20-plus years is that the overwhelming majority of those patients do well.
sentences.zh: 找到了一位与你配合良好的外科医生，我20多年的经验是，绝大多数这样的病人都会做得很好。

sentences.en: That doesn't mean everyone should be doing it.
sentences.zh: 但这并不意味着每个人都应该去做。

sentences.en: But conversely, there are absolutely people that shouldn't be doing it that are seeking it, and who are those people?
sentences.zh: 但反过来说，确实有人不应该做却在寻求手术，那么这些人是谁呢？

sentences.en: And I tend to be a bit more transparent.
sentences.zh: 我倾向于更透明一点。

sentences.en: If you follow me on social media, you listen to my podcasts, everything and anything that comes out of my mouth is cautionary.
sentences.zh: 如果你关注我的社交媒体，听我的播客，我口中说出的任何话都是警示性的。

sentences.en: I live and die.
sentences.zh: 我以此为生。

sentences.en: I'm sort of the Howard Stern meets Geraldo and the, you know, reportive investigator of plastic surgeons.
sentences.zh: 我有点像是霍华德·斯特恩（Howard Stern）遇上杰拉尔多（Geraldo），是整形外科医生的调查员。

sentences.en: I'm the guy that everyone keeps sending DMs to, like, hey, should I do this procedure?
sentences.zh: 我是那个每个人都发私信问我：“嘿，我该做这个手术吗？”的人。

sentences.en: This sounds fishy.
sentences.zh: 这听起来很可疑。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不。

sentences.en: So these are the things that would be a concern to me.
sentences.zh: 所以这些就是让我担心的事情。

sentences.en: Number one is when a patient comes in to you and says how much they dislike something, they describe it to you in great detail, how much, how terrible it is.
sentences.zh: 第一点是，当病人来找你，说他们有多讨厌某样东西，详细描述它有多糟糕，

sentences.en: And when you look at them, you simply just don't see it.
sentences.zh: 而当你看着他们时，你根本看不出来。

sentences.en: Like, I genuinely don't know what you're talking about.
sentences.zh: 就像，我真的不知道你在说什么。

sentences.en: A perfect example is a girl that came in just today who wanted a nose job, a revision nose job.
sentences.zh: 一个完美的例子是今天刚来的一个女孩，她想要做隆鼻手术，修复性隆鼻。

sentences.en: And at the end, I said, listen, I have to tell you, I think your nose looks great.
sentences.zh: 最后我说，听着，我必须告诉你，我觉得你的鼻子看起来很棒。

sentences.en: It has a little bump on it and a little this.
sentences.zh: 它有一点点凸起，有一点点这个那个。

sentences.en: But those things are, like, minor.
sentences.zh: 但那些东西，怎么说呢，很小。

sentences.en: By and large, you look good.
sentences.zh: 总的来说，你看起来很好。

sentences.en: I wouldn't touch it.
sentences.zh: 我不会动它。

sentences.en: So red flag number one is what they see, you don't see.
sentences.zh: 所以第一个危险信号就是：他们看到的，你没看到。

sentences.en: Right?
sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: If my son comes to me who's four years old and says, Papa, Papa, do you see the monster?
sentences.zh: 如果我四岁的儿子跑来对我说：“爸爸，爸爸，你看到那个怪物了吗？”

sentences.en: And I'm like, I don't know what you're talking about, Bubba.
sentences.zh: 而我说：“我不知道你在说什么，宝贝。”

sentences.en: You know, I don't see what you see.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我没看到你看到的。

sentences.en: Second thing that's a red flag is when they make it seem as though this issue is really the end all be all.
sentences.zh: 第二个危险信号是，当他们表现得好像这个问题真的是生死攸关一样。

sentences.en: It's going to change their lives.
sentences.zh: 这会改变他们的生活。

sentences.en: They apply too much emphasis on something.
sentences.zh: 他们对某件事赋予了太多的重要性。

sentences.en: You can tell that psychologically they've attached too much value to this item.
sentences.zh: 你可以看出他们在心理上对这个项目赋予了太高的价值。

sentences.en: Right?
sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: And while I think changing the way you look creates a sense of confidence, which then bleeds into your personal relationships.
sentences.zh: 虽然我认为改变外貌会产生一种自信，进而影响到你的人际关系。

sentences.en: I cannot tell you the countless number of people who have had surgeries and as a result have massively kindled their interpersonal relationships with their loved ones,
sentences.zh: 我无法告诉你，有多少人做过手术后，极大地改善了他们与亲人、

sentences.en: their boyfriends, their girlfriends, their husbands, their wives.
sentences.zh: 男朋友、女朋友、丈夫、妻子的关系。

sentences.en: But when you're making it sound like this is going to change your life, like you just got, you know, I don't know, brain transplant, that's a concern.
sentences.zh: 但当你把它说得好像这会改变你的人生，就像你刚做了个什么脑移植手术一样，那就有问题了。

sentences.en: When patients don't track the risks when you talk to them, I'm very under-promise, over-deliver kind.
sentences.zh: 当病人在你和他们谈论风险时，他们不当回事。我属于那种“承诺较少，交付较多”的人。

sentences.en: I'm very like, and then this can happen, and then this can happen, and then you could be paralyzed, and then you could die.
sentences.zh: 我非常强调“这可能会发生，那可能会发生，你可能会瘫痪，你可能会死”。

sentences.en: Like, I'm very much doomsday, because I like to push the dooms, because if you go through the doomsday conversation, you're still on board.
sentences.zh: 我非常像个末日预言者，因为我喜欢把最坏的情况推到极致，如果你听完了末日对话还坚持要做，

sentences.en: It means that, you know, you understand the real risks.
sentences.zh: 那就意味着你理解真正的风险。

sentences.en: But when they actually act like nothing, like they don't register it, it's a concern to me that they're not going to follow through.
sentences.zh: 但当他们表现得好像什么都没发生，完全没听进去时，我担心他们不会遵医嘱。

sentences.en: When they have any type of psychological condition, whether they have borderline disorder, they're very jittery, dismissive, they're very labile in their emotions, they're crying,
sentences.zh: 当他们有任何类型的心理状况时，无论是边缘性人格障碍，他们非常紧张、轻率，情绪非常不稳定，又哭又笑，

sentences.en: and then they're excited, they're angry, and then they're depressed.
sentences.zh: 然后又兴奋、愤怒，接着又抑郁。

sentences.en: Any type of mood swings, I won't do.
sentences.zh: 任何类型的情绪波动，我都不会做。

sentences.en: And when they're asking for things that are extreme, that I just, like, if you're 5'2", and you weigh 125 pounds, and you're an A-cup, and you bring me a photo of some huge star,
sentences.zh: 还有当他们要求极端的东西时，比如你身高5英尺2英寸，体重125磅，A罩杯，你拿给我看一张某个巨星的照片，

sentences.en: and you're like, I want these massive boobs, it's like, and there's no way that's going to happen.
sentences.zh: 然后说“我想要这种巨大的乳房”，这根本不可能实现。

sentences.en: So, remember, I don't want to be entangled in a marriage with someone with a bad outcome.
sentences.zh: 所以，记住，我不想因为糟糕的结果而陷入一段“婚姻”中。

sentences.en: So, as much as it is my responsibility to prevent them from doing it, I don't want to get involved in this with you,
sentences.zh: 所以，虽然我有责任阻止他们这样做，但我不想和你卷入其中，

sentences.en: because you're ultimately going to be a patient who's going to be dissatisfied or unhappy or not have a good outcome.
sentences.zh: 因为你最终会成为一个不满、不开心或结果不好的病人。

sentences.en: So, I spend a lot of time trying to make sure that I marry the right people, because once I operate on you, you're my forever responsibility, right?
sentences.zh: 所以我花了很多时间确保我“嫁”对了人，因为一旦我为你做了手术，你就是我永远的责任，对吧？

sentences.en: It's not like I sold you a bag, a handbag at the mall, and you're unhappy, and you return it.
sentences.zh: 这不像我在商场卖给你一个包，你不喜欢，然后退货。

sentences.en: You're like, this bag sucks.
sentences.zh: 你说：“这包太烂了。”

sentences.en: You're like, okay, here, buddy, here's your money back.
sentences.zh: 然后我说：“好吧，伙计，钱退给你。”

sentences.en: Just be well.
sentences.zh: 祝你一切安好。

sentences.en: This is kind of like we're forever tied.
sentences.zh: 这更像是我们永远捆绑在一起了。

sentences.en: So, I am very cautionary about making sure that the patients have realistic and doable expectations, and they're emotionally stable and seem to be present in that moment.
sentences.zh: 所以我非常谨慎，确保病人的期望是现实且可行的，并且他们情绪稳定，看起来活在当下。

sentences.en: I want to hone in on the second point you said here, because I think this is interesting, and I feel like the listeners will want me to talk about this a bit.
sentences.zh: 我想深入探讨你刚才说的第二点，因为我觉得这很有趣，我觉得听众也会想让我多谈谈这个。

sentences.en: But the patient who is like, this is going to be the thing that changes my life, why, for them, would you not operate on that kind of person?
sentences.zh: 对于那些说“这将是我改变人生的契机”的病人，为什么你不会为这样的人做手术？

sentences.en: Do you think it's because there's a deeper psychological insecurity going on or a deeper relationship with their body that surgery can't fix?
